claims.text: Introducing reactive wear protection can improve the wear resistance of high-entropy-alloy coatings.
The proposed improvement will persist from room temperature to 800 °C.
Reactive wear protection will form an oxide nanocomposite surface during wear.
The resulting oxide nanocomposite surface will be both strong and deformable.
A strong and deformable oxide nanocomposite surface provides a reactive wear-protection mechanism.
The intervention will reduce wear rate by at least 50% relative to an otherwise identical unmodified high-entropy-alloy coating.
An unmodified high-entropy-alloy coating is the appropriate baseline for evaluating the intervention.
The proposed wear-resistance improvement is bounded at temperatures above 800 °C.
The mechanism and its effectiveness may vary with alloy composition and processing state.
Wear rate and surface morphology can be compared between protected and unmodified coatings from room temperature to 800 °C.
Failure of the protected coating to exhibit a significantly lower wear rate than the unmodified coating would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 50% wear-rate reduction, whereas the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant reduction. A significant reduction smaller than 50% would satisfy the experiment's success criterion but fail the stated quantitative prediction.
